notAnIdeology.explanation: Britannica, Mylonas and Tudor (Annual Review of Political Science) and Wikipedia define nation-building as a process: states or outside powers building institutions and a shared national identity through schooling, media, symbols and language, by accommodation, assimilation or exclusion alike. I went through the statements on the state's role, culture, ethnic nation, secession, immigration, force abroad and democracy and found no position these sources state as part of it, so fewer than two can be answered; what they record is practices and their varying results, and what critics argue (imperialism, erased regional cultures) is about what such projects did.

sources.title: Nationalism: What We Know and What We Still Need to Know | Annual Reviews
